messages.content: "你能幫我幾件事嗎？首先，我想知道2010年演員李奧納多·狄卡皮歐主演的所有電影，尤其是在戲劇類別中的作品。其次，我想了解在2015年位於加州的“蘋果公司”是否有任何訴訟，我尤其感興趣的是民事案件。最後，我需要預訂一張從“紐約”到“倫敦”的直航航班，日期為“2022-12-25”，我希望時間大約在“上午10:00”。你能幫我處理這些嗎？"

function.name: lawsuits_search

function.name: flight_book
function.description: Book a direct flight for a specific date and time from departure location to destination location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

destination_location.description: The location you are flying to.

time.description: Preferred time of flight. Format XX:XXAM or XX:XXPM. Default ''

direct_flight.description: If set to true, only direct flights will be searched. Default is false

function.name: imdb_find_movies_by_actor
function.description: Searches the database to find all movies by a specific actor within a certain year. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

year.description: The specific year to search in.

category.description: The category of the film (e.g. Drama, Comedy, etc). This parameter is optional. Default is all if not specified.

message.reasoning:
The user wants three tasks:

1. Find all movies starring Leonardo DiCaprio in 2010, especially drama category.

2. Search for civil lawsuits involving "Apple Inc." in California in 2015.

3. Book a direct flight from New York to London on 2022-12-25 around 10:00 AM.

We have two functions: lawsuits_search and flight_book. There's also imdb_find_movies_by_actor. So we need to call each function accordingly.

We should do them sequentially. We can call imdb_find_movies_by_actor with actor_name="Leonardo DiCaprio", year=2010, category="Drama". Then call lawsuits_search with company_name="Apple Inc.", location="California", year=2015, case_type="civil". Then call flight_book with departure_location="New York", destination_location="London", date="2022-12-25", time="10:00AM", direct_flight=True.

We need to output calls to the function. According to guidelines, we should use the function calls. We'll produce separate calls. Probably we need to call them one after another. Let's do it.
